clue.text: Complete louts on the rampage in Lincoln

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, enclosed by the president's name

parts.note: Abe is the nickname of US president Abraham Lincoln

indicators.note: a rampaging mob runs wild, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Hooligans run riot in the English city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the cathedral city, but it is the president, Abe; the rearranged louts sit between AB and E to make ABSOLUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute and complete are synonyms, both meaning total, entire or unqualified.

clue.text: Admit carbon copy record in a first trial

indicators.note: these pieces are placed inside the outer letters

parts.note: taken as written
cc stands for carbon copy, as on emails
an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: Evidence, a copy and a recording, is admitted at a first trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a first trial' supplies the outer pair, A and the T of trial, around the copy and the record.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something is to acknowledge or agree that it is true, which is to admit it.

clue.text: Son left university at last keen on games

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: at the last means only the final letter is taken

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A son finally left university, being more interested in sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb but is the nautical side, PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sporty is fond of and good at athletic pursuits, so keen on games fits.

clue.text: Become very angry and look ready to get hold of me

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: to get hold of something is to grip it, enclosing it within

parts.note: set means ready, as in ready, steady, go
I is the speaker, me

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper and looks set to grab the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: LO is an archaic interjection meaning look, as in lo and behold.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose it is an informal idiom for losing self-control, typically by flying into a rage.

clue.text: Children's fantasy character is beautiful, young and, above all, also extremely tough

indicators.note: in a down entry, above all places these pieces on top of everything else

parts.note: too means also

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: its first and last letters
fair is an old word for beautiful
Y is the abbreviation for young

explanation.surface: A storybook character described as lovely, youthful and tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'above all' is a positional instruction: in a down answer, the last pieces named go on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The tooth fairy is the imaginary figure who leaves money for children's lost milk teeth.

clue.text: Vacancies for experts after sponsorship ends

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
aces are people highly skilled at something

explanation.surface: Job openings for skilled people appear once the sponsorship money dries up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' means both ends of the word, not just the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacancies are empty places or gaps, so spaces is a straightforward synonym for unfilled room.

clue.text: Writer represented Nike protecting fellow in small cutter

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it to keep it safe
re-presented means set out again in a different form, so the brand name is rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: An author signed by Nike, shielding a colleague in a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' looks like a small boat; here it is a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A penknife is a small folding pocket knife, originally used for sharpening quills.

clue.text: On filling initial curriculum vitae, set out to be original

indicators.note: a filling goes inside, so this piece is put within the rest
setting out is laying out afresh, so these letters are rearranged
the initial of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter
the fodder, taken as written
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: Advice on filling in a CV so that it stands out as original.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curriculum vitae' looks like one phrase, but its first word gives one letter and its second is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Creative and original both describe thinking that is inventive and imaginative rather than imitative.

clue.text: Noticeably different leading actor in TV role

parts.note: a TV is a television set

indicators.note: the leading letter of a word is its first

parts.note: its first letter
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: A star actor in a television role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading actor' looks like a star, but leading takes only the A; TV comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Set apart means distinguished from others, standing out as distinct or noticeably different.

clue.text: Crucifix with bend in arm

parts.note: a crucifix is a cross bearing the figure of Christ
to bow is to bend the body forward

explanation.surface: A crucifix held in the crook of a bent arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' looks like the body part, but it means a weapon, as in firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a weapon, and an arm in the sense of weaponry covers any such device.

clue.text: First half of injury time sees City come in and shoot

indicators.note: something that comes in enters and sits inside the rest
only the opening half of the six-letter word is kept

parts.note: the first three of its six letters
T is the standard abbreviation for time
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A football report: in first-half injury time a City player comes on and shoots.
explanation.walkthrough: City is not a football club but the City of London, whose postcode is EC.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot up is slang for injecting a drug, so shoot can stand for inject.

clue.text: Shot on green, briefly to one side, straightened out

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a putt is a golf stroke played on the green
right is one of the two sides

explanation.surface: A golfer's putt drifts off to one side before being corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: PUTT loses its final T to give PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something right is to correct or fix it, matching straightened out as a past-tense verb.

clue.text: Heading off on piste, broke part of foot

indicators.note: removing the head of a word drops its first letter
broken letters are smashed apart and put back in a new order

parts.note: the little word loses its first letter
taken as written: a ski run

explanation.surface: A skier sets off down the run and breaks a bone in their foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The instep is the arched middle section of the human foot between toes and ankle.

clue.text: Flopped when champagne taken away?

parts.note: fizz is informal for champagne
led out means escorted away

explanation.surface: A party falls flat once the champagne is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: fizz led out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that fizzles out ends feebly and fails, just as a venture that flopped did.

clue.text: Distress when stuck inside taxi home with father hugging girl

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap your arms round, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
to be in is to be at home
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
a stock crossword girl's name

explanation.surface: A taxi ride home with Dad holding a girl tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'father' is abbreviated as for a priest, Fr, and it is that abbreviation which does the hugging.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabin fever is the restless irritability felt when confined indoors for a long period.

clue.text: Key worker's supporting sailor's international body is more than enough

indicators.note: in a down entry, a support lies underneath, so this piece goes below the rest

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
the UN is the United Nations
D is a musical key
a worker ant is a stock crossword worker

explanation.surface: An essential worker backing a sailors' international organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key worker' looks like one phrase, an essential employee, but splits into a musical key and an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant means plentiful, existing in large quantities, so more than enough is a fair paraphrase.

clue.text: King abandons game having note from flirtatious lady

indicators.note: the abbreviation walks out and leaves the word without it

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game with mallets and hoops
R is Rex, Latin for king
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A monarch quits a lawn game after a note from a flirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Croquet is a lawn game in which balls are knocked through hoops with mallets.
explanation.definitionFit: A coquette is a woman who flirts playfully to win admiration without serious intent.

clue.text: Unexpectedly, Bach work's unknown within northern church

indicators.note: within places this letter inside the rearranged name
the composer's name is worked, that is fashioned into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
y is a mathematical unknown
N is the abbreviation for northern
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A surprise discovery of an unknown Bach work in a northern church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' looks like a composition but is the anagram signal; Y sits inside the rearranged BACH.
explanation.definitionFit: By chance means by accident or without planning, so something happening unexpectedly happens by chance.

clue.text: Idiot, finishing sulkily, spoils reward for last place

parts.note: a boob is a foolish person, as in booby

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter

parts.note: its last letter
spoils are plunder taken as a prize

explanation.surface: A sulky fool ruins things, the picture of a sore loser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' looks like a verb but is the noun, the loot won.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby prize is a joke award given to whoever comes bottom of a competition.

clue.text: Very happy with politician embracing a top deal with European Union

indicators.note: embracing means wrapping round, so the politician encloses the other pieces

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter
EU is the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A politician delighted to secure a top-class deal with the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top deal' looks like a great bargain, but top takes only the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Made up is informal British, especially northern, slang for thrilled or delighted.

clue.text: Some feel Cricklewood's about to get a London Underground line

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the run reads backwards
some means only part of the words is taken, a run of letters

parts.note: a run straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Cricklewood residents feel they are about to get a Tube line.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricklewood is a district of north-west London, which makes the Tube surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Circle line is one of the London Underground's routes, looping round central London.

clue.text: Leeds team announced second person to be given an honour

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the words count by their sound

parts.note: you is the second-person pronoun
to be knighted is to receive an honour from the monarch

explanation.surface: A football club's announcement that a player is to be honoured.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'you knighted' runs together into the club's nickname. Leeds United is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds United is the professional football club of Leeds, commonly shortened to just United.

clue.text: Fear abandoning old battleship for nothing

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave behind, so those letters are dropped from the rest

parts.note: the Dreadnought was a famous early twentieth-century battleship type
dread is great fear

explanation.surface: Abandoning an old warship out of fear, for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: DREADNOUGHT minus DREAD leaves NOUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nought is zero, the figure representing an absence of quantity, so it equals nothing.

clue.text: Annoyance with former partner replacing account during holiday

indicators.note: one thing replacing another takes its place, swapping one set of letters out

parts.note: vacation is a holiday, especially in American usage
AC is the abbreviation for account
an ex is a former spouse or partner

explanation.surface: The irritation of meeting your ex on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: In VACATION, the AC is swapped out for EX.
explanation.definitionFit: Vexation is irritation or annoyance, the state of being troubled by something.

clue.text: Pretending to be about to retire can start to gall

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: ca is circa, Latin for about
a tin is a can

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: Faking it about being ready to retire may be galling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like the verb but is the container, TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting means putting on a performance or feigning, which is what pretending is.

clue.text: Command less authority, when without electricity?

definitions.note: a phrase read cryptically, not a synonym
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: a reduction in power

definitions.note: describes the state rather than naming the event
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a failure of the electrical supply

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads as an instruction to wield less authority; split differently, a cut in power is just that.
explanation.definitionFit: A power cut is an interruption of the mains electricity supply, leaving homes in the dark.

clue.text: Picked up drink to go in tent

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so the words are judged by ear

parts.note: tea is a drink
to go is a euphemism for urinating

explanation.surface: Having a drink and then needing a toilet while camping in a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go' is the coy phrase for needing the loo.
explanation.definitionFit: A teepee is a conical tent of skins or canvas used by Native American peoples of the Plains.

clue.text: Returning vessels very suddenly come to a halt

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so it is read backwards

parts.note: pots are vessels for cooking or holding things
dead means very, as in dead easy

explanation.surface: Ships coming back into port suddenly halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' suggests ships but means pots; only POTS is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop dead is an idiom for halting abruptly and completely, without slowing first.
